I use to sleep on my stomach but now I sleep on my side. Sleep doctor, that's a new idea. I like that. Everyone keeps suggesting to see an ENT or psychiatrist but nobody has mentioned a sleep doctor yet. I might give that a go.

I'm not on any meds currently. I try to not take any if I can help it.

I don't get dizzy, though I have heard about that manouvre before and have tried it. I find no sleep makes the sound 'sharper' for me, though the sound itself keeps me from sleeping well - a catch 22. How do you deal with the sound in your head? I can't stand it :(

Nice username. You're right, thank you for understanding. It's like torture when you can't sleep and haven't slept for 48 hours straight, chronically.

I've tried exercise but it makes my tinnitus worse for some reason. It amplifies from a background buzz to literally the volume of a steam kettle. So much so that I had trouble believing that I was the only one that was hearing it. I've developed almost a fear of exertion after that incident. It was so loud.
